/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 25 September 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3426 (-47)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5784 (-155)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2407 (25)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1786 (4)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1011 (8)
CAPESIZE
The Capesize market came off recent highs and lost some momentum on the final day of the week across both basins. Nevertheless, the BCI 182 5TC edged up $142 week-on-week to close at $52,457. In the Atlantic, both transatlantic and fronthaul rates took a breather today as softer fixtures emerged towards the end of the week. The C8 route retreated by more than $1,000 to $62,938, although it remained at its strongest level since early December last year. The C9 index followed a similar pattern, easing back to finish the week at $91,494. In the Pacific, the C5 index came under pressure once again, falling to $15.625 following a succession of fixtures reported at this level.

Atlantic
A vessel from Oldendorff was linked to LKAB’s 135,000/150,000 Narvik to Djen-Djen 7/16 October at a rate in the mid $21s.

Asia
Rio Tinto fixed 170,000/10 Dampier to Qingdao 13/15 October at $15.60 today. Last night, the ES Glory Sea (177,814 2007) was fixed to LSS for 150,000/10 Southeast Kalimantan to Mundra 6/12 October in the mid $12s. JFE’s tender of 170,000/10 Port Hedland to Qingdao 9/14 October was fixed at $17.50.
PANAMAX
Today saw a further improvement in sentiment, with the P5TC increasing by $228 to close the week at $21,662. The trans-Atlantic market continued to build on yesterday's gains, with brokers reporting stronger mineral demand while market sources highlighted a growing disparity between longer and shorter duration voyage rates. Fronthaul sentiment also remained well supported, with the influx of trans-Atlantic stems helping to reduce available tonnage and tighten supply fundamentals. In the Pacific, activity was described as quieter due to several national holidays across the basin, although overall sentiment remained positive. Demand from Australia was highlighted as particularly active, helping to underpin market levels despite the slower trading environment. The Aris (95,629 2012) open Tonda 2 October was reported to have been placed on subjects for a trip via Australia to Japan with a cargo of coal in the $22,000s to Kline. The Xing Shun Hai (81,824 2018) open Yeosu 30 September was reported fixed, although no further details emerged. Elsewhere, Ming Wah were said to have taken the Guang Bo (82,245 2023) open Guangdong 1 October for a one-year period at a rate reported by some sources to be around $21,700.
SUPRAMAX
After a relatively flat week, the 11TC average showed another small gain of $54 to finish the week at $22,579, up $247 from last weeks close. With a South Korean holiday today, and after a week of holidays elsewhere in Asia, there were understandably few trades circulating although sentiment has remained positive. The SSI Discovery (63,712 2023) Koh Sichang 24-29 September was reportedly fixed for trip via New Caledonia back to the Far East with nickel ore at $25,000 with WBC, however a source suggested the rate had been much lower, and the Vega (55,733 2011) Cai Mep 1-2 October was fixed for a trip to Bangladesh with clinker at $30,000 to an unnamed Charterer. The Alam Sayang (61,353 2013) fixed basis delivery Paradip for a coastal trip with iron ore redelivery East coast at $20,500 and in the Mediterranean a 53,000-dwt open Diliskelesi was said to have fixed via Constanza to Bangladesh with redelivery passing Singapore at $15,000, but in both cases the Charterer was not reported. There were a few rumours of US Gulf trades, but details were lacking, making in difficult to ascertain when they were fixed. A 64,000-dwt was said to have fixed a coal stem to the East Mediterranean at $33,500, a 62,000-dwt was said to have fixed grains business to China at $33,000 and a 61,000-dwt fixed US East Coast to East Mediterranean with grains, also at $33,000.
HANDYSIZE
The week concluded on an overall positive note, with optimism prevailing across both basins. The BHSI increased by 8 points to 1,011, while the 7TC average gained $129 to settle at $18,190. In the South Atlantic and US Gulf, activity remained limited, although sentiment was firm and only marginal rate adjustments were seen on some routes. In contrast, the Continent and Mediterranean remained particularly strong, with rates continuing to rise. The Ise Bay (40,101 2024) open Iskenderun on 27–28 September was fixed for delivery Mediterranean and a trip to EC Mexico at close to $15,000. The Inoi (32,301 2010) open Vatika Bay on 24 September was fixed by Martrade for a trip to the UK with pipes at around $12,750, although further details were not disclosed. The Pacific market remained steady, although regional holidays continued to limit activity. Some sources noted an increase in available tonnage, while rates under discussion remained at healthy levels.

Market Fundamentals
World Crude Steel Production
World crude steel production in August stood 1.2% below the same month last year at 144.2 Mt, World Steel Association data show. The decline was driven by Asia, where production dropped 1.3% to 106.2 Mt, as a 3.7% fall in Chinese output to 74.6 Mt more than offset gains in India (+4.6% to 14.8 Mt) and Vietnam (+36.4% to 2.7 Mt). In the same period, North American production edged up 3.9% to 9.4 Mt, while EU output fell 1.0% to 8.9 Mt.

US Steel Imports
US steel imports rose 0.4 Mt on the year to 2.1 Mt in August, US Census Bureau data show. Shipments from South Korea doubled to 0.4 Mt, bringing year-to-August volumes 0.9 Mt above year-on-year at 2.7 Mt and higher than full year 2025 total. However, total US shipments in the year-to-August fell 2.5 Mt to 14.4 Mt following a decline to Canada and Brazil.
Sent from Front

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape was sharply weaker today, with heavy activity across October and the front quarters. October opened around 48,000–48,250 before steadily weakening through 47,500, 46,500 and eventually 45,500, where significant late volume traded. November followed the move lower, falling from around 46,000 to 44,000 and later 43,850. December traded around 43,350–43,450. Q4 26 weakened from 45,400–45,500 to around 44,000, while Q1 27 fell from 31,600 to around 31,000. Q2 27 traded down from 35,400 to 35,250 before recovering slightly. Cal 27 traded 33,250–33,500, while Cal 28 eased from 28,000 to 27,900. Overall, the curve came under significant pressure, led by October, November and Q1 27.

FIXING STARTED EARLY IN THE MORNING AT 20,500 BKI AND BY THE END OF THE DAY HAD RISEN TO 21,750 BKI CJK FOR EAUS/CHINA. THIS WAS A LARGER JUMP THAN MOST HAD EXPECTED. THE EAUS MARKET CONTINUED TO BE THE MAIN DRIVER OF THE PACIFIC MARKET THIS WEEK, WITH CHINESE BUYERS LOOKING TO TAKE COVER AHEAD OF THE MID-AUTUMN FESTIVAL. BY WEDNESDAY AND THURSDAY, FIXTURES HAD RISEN TO THE 23,000 BKI CJK LEVEL FOR MORE FORWARD UNITS AND THE MID-HIGH 22,000S FOR VESSELS OPENING OVER THE WEEKEND. DESPITE THE JAPANESE BEING ON HOLIDAY FOR THE FIRST HALF OF THE WEEK, THERE WAS ENOUGH CHINESE BUYING PRESENCE TO KEEP THE MARKET POSITIVE. SPOT UNITS WERE STEADILY CLEARED AND CHARTS WERE FIXING AT INCREASINGLY FIRMER LEVELS AHEAD OF THE HOLIDAYS. DEMAND REPLENISHMENT ALSO REMAINED FAIRLY STRONG THROUGHOUT THE WEEK SO THE EAUS MARKET IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN RELATIVELY WELL SUPPORTED GOING INTO NEXT WEEK. THE NOPAC CARGO LIST REMAINED STABLE AND WAS NOT A MAJOR DRIVER OF THE PACIFIC MARKET THIS WEEK. THE WEEK OPENED WITH GENERIC BIDS AROUND 20,000-20,500 BKI AND THIS REMAINED FAIRLY CONSISTENT THROUGHOUT THE WEEK. FIXTURES WERE NOT PARTICULARLY ABUNDANT BUT UNITS WERE CONCLUDED IN THE 21,000-21,500 RANGE THROUGHOUT THE WEEK. THERE DOES NOT APPEAR TO BE MUCH REASON FOR THIS TO CHANGE IN THE SHORT TERM. THE INDO MARKET WAS LARGELY DOMINATED BY INDIA REPOSITIONING CARGOES THROUGHOUT THE WEEK. THE WEEK OPENED WITH MORE THAN HALF OF THE CARGO REQUIREMENTS FOCUSED ON CHINA/INDIA AND INDIA/INDIA WHICH RESULTED IN THE LATTER TRIP PAYING A PREMIUM. INDO/CHINA WAS STILL FIXING IN THE MID-HIGH 17,000S BKI HK BY TUESDAY COMPARED WITH AROUND 20,000 BKI HK FOR INDO/INDIA. BY WEDNESDAY AND THURSDAY WE STARTED TO SEE CHINESE BUYERS ENTER THE MARKET BUT THEY WERE PRIMARILY FOCUSED ON OA LME’S WHICH WERE FIXING IN THE LOW-MID TEENS. INDO/PHILIPPINES, USUALLY A KEY DRIVER FOR THE INDO MARKET, REMAINED RELATIVELY SUBDUED WITH CARGOES EVENTUALLY HAVING TO FIX A TICK BELOW 20,000 BKI HK. WITH THE MID-AUTUMN FESTIVAL STARTING TODAY, WE DO NOT EXPECT THE INDO/CHINA MARKET TO BE PARTICULARLY BUSY GOING INTO THE COMING WEEK BUT LEVELS SHOULD REMAIN RELATIVELY STABLE AND ARE NOT EXPECTED TO DECLINE SIGNIFICANTLY. THE OVERALL MARKET VIEW GOING INTO NEXT WEEK IS ONE OF STABILITY. THE TONNAGE LIST HAS GRADUALLY CLEARED THROUGHOUT THE WEEK WHILE CARGO REPLENISHMENT HAS REMAINED STEADY. WITH THE EAUS MARKET CONTINUING TO PROVIDE SUPPORT AND THE OVERALL TONNAGE POSITION TIGHTENING, WE EXPECT THE PACIFIC MARKET TO REMAIN RELATIVELY WELL SUPPORTED GOING INTO NEXT WEEK.
